title: What If You Threw Away a Hard Drive Holding 8,000 Bitcoin? One Man Did

scenes.text: What if you binned a hard drive worth hundreds of millions of dollars? In 2013, it happened.
A man in Wales had mined 8,000 bitcoin in 2009, when they were worth almost nothing. The key sat on an old drive.
In August 2013, during a clear-out, the drive went to the city dump by mistake.
As bitcoin soared, he proposed a dig with AI scanners and robot dogs, and offered the council a share. It refused.
In January 2025, with the coins worth about 750 million dollars, a judge threw out his claim.
The reason: by law, anything left at the dump belongs to the council. In 2025, he gave up on digging.

description:
What if you threw away a hard drive holding 8,000 bitcoin? In August 2013 a drive with the private key to coins mined in 2009 went to the Docksway landfill in Newport, Wales, during a home-office clear-out.
Its owner spent years asking Newport City Council for permission to excavate, offering it a share and proposing a search with AI sorting, drones and robot dogs costing 10 to 11 million pounds. On 9 January 2025 a High Court judge dismissed his claim as having no realistic prospect of succeeding: under a 1974 law, anything delivered to the site belongs to the council. The coins were then worth roughly 750 million dollars. In August 2025 he said he was no longer pursuing an excavation. This is a news story, not financial advice.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: The court accepted that he still owns the bitcoin. He just does not own the drive that unlocks them. What would you have done? Drop your own what-if below.
